=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md): Step 0 child bullet "Issue-mode resume without a — resume. block" (line 12), Step 1 (line 15), cleanup section header (line 187). | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The issue-mode cleanup is deferred until Step 1 reads the plan, but the cited reviews report that Step 1 does not invoke it and the cleanup header still assigns it to Step 0.
  WHY: An unattended resume may attempt cleanup before the `Source issue:` identifier is available or never invoke it after Step 1, leaving the stopped stage session unarchived; minimax_minimax-m3 reports that the current diff adds the Step 1 trigger and updates the header.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md): Renaming (set_session_title) and label-read (mcp__github__issue_read) logic. | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The renaming and label-read logic lacks failure-handling paths for transient errors.
  WHY: A rename failure can leave the old title unmatched by cleanup, and a label-read failure can skip archival without logging or reporting.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: lines 12 and 16 (new Step 0 bullet plus Step 1 trigger) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The Step 0 bullet and Step 1 trigger both imperatively describe the cleanup, which may lead an unattended session to attempt it before Step 1 has parsed the plan.
  WHY: The Step 0 wording may prompt a premature cleanup attempt before the `Source issue:` identifier is available; the cited review notes that the current diff also adds an explicit Step 1 trigger.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 192 (cleanup-section report line: "Zombie checkers archived: <n>, plus `stopped stage sessions archived: <m>` in issue mode") | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup report does not distinguish a project-mode resume that intentionally skips the issue-mode sweep from an issue-mode run that matched no stopped sessions.
  WHY: The cited review says the chat-only report leaves those two skip paths indistinguishable; qwen_qwen3_7-plus reports the current diff documents the non-issue-mode skip as intentional.
- tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py: line 260, the assertion `"blocked on issue" not in text.replace("— blocked on issue", "")` | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The collision check does not prevent a future slug or stage name from producing a session title that matches the cleanup's `blocked on issue` suffix predicate.
  WHY: A future title containing that literal could be archived even though it is not an issue-mode stop, while the contract test still passes.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md)
  Line or code reference: Step 0 child bullet "Issue-mode resume without a — resume. block" (line 12), Step 1 (line 15), cleanup section header (line 187).
  PROBLEM: Logical contradiction between the Step 0 bullet, the Step 1 execution flow, and the cleanup section header. The Step 0 bullet defers cleanup to Step 1, but Step 1 does not invoke it, and the cleanup header at line 187 still assigns it to Step 0.
  WHY: An unattended session following the instructions will either attempt cleanup in Step 0 (where the Source issue identifier is missing, so it fails/skips) or defer it to Step 1 (where it is never invoked), leaving the stopped stage session unarchived.
  severity=BLOCKER | confidence=[5]
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md)
  Line or code reference: Renaming (set_session_title) and label-read (mcp__github__issue_read) logic.
  PROBLEM: Lack of failure-handling paths for transient errors in renaming or label reading.
  WHY: A rename failure can leave the session with its old title (which cleanup won't match), and a label-read failure can skip archival without logging/reporting, necessitating manual cleanup.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]

  Evidence of absence: Step 1 (line 15) contains no reference to the Zombie-checker cleanup. Cleanup section header at line 187 remains unchanged ("Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene"), which is the opposite of the issue-mode timing needed; no operational hook fires the cleanup where the Step 0 bullet's text says it should happen.
  severity=BLOCKER | confidence=[5]
- Requirement: A contract test must pin the issue-mode cleanup trigger's placement after Step 1 reads the plan and verify the cleanup section header distinguishes issue-mode timing, so a future edit cannot silently regress the trigger.
  Expected change site: tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py
  Evidence of absence: The existing test (test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions) only asserts text-string existence; it does not assert that Step 1 references the cleanup, does not assert the cleanup-section header distinguishes issue-mode timing, and does not pin the deferred cleanup to an operational hook after Step 1.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
- Requirement: The lint check (tests/inventory_parity.py) must pass for the PR to merge; scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py must be documented in the docs/INVENTORY.md Scripts section or explicitly exempted in tests/inventory_exemptions.txt.
  Expected change site: docs/INVENTORY.md (Scripts section) or tests/inventory_exemptions.txt
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff does not touch docs/INVENTORY.md to include scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py; tests/inventory_parity.py fails on this PR head, blocking the merge.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: lines 12 and 16 (new Step 0 bullet plus Step 1 trigger)
  PROBLEM: The new Step 0 bullet ("once step 1 has read the plan, run the [Zombie-checker cleanup] too") is phrased as an imperative with a temporal precondition, while Step 1 also carries an explicit imperative trigger ("run the [Zombie-checker cleanup] now, right after this read and before step 2"). Two imperatives that both describe the same action increase the chance a future unattended session will execute cleanup in Step 0 before Step 1 has parsed the plan, find no `Source issue:` line, and silently fall through — exactly the failure mode the original PR description cites as cause 2.
  WHY: A session that walks the steps literally sees "run the cleanup" as a Step 0 instruction (preconditioned), attempts it, finds no source issue, and falls through. The Step 1 instruction is still there, but the Step 0 wording invites the wrong turn. The cross-pollination summary shows this exact contradiction was the BLOCKER in earlier rounds; the current diff fixes it on the Step 1 side but keeps the ambiguous wording on the Step 0 side.
  severity=NIT | confidence=[3]
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: line 192 (cleanup-section report line: "Zombie checkers archived: <n>, plus `stopped stage sessions archived: <m>` in issue mode")
  PROBLEM: A project-mode resume (plan without `Source issue:`) executes the cleanup and emits a report that still says "Zombie checkers archived: <n>, plus stopped stage sessions archived: <m> in issue mode" with `m` simply omitted. An operator reading the chat-only report cannot distinguish (a) "we ran in project mode, so the issue-mode sweep was intentionally skipped" from (b) "we were in issue mode but no `… — blocked on issue` session matched". The Step 0 bullet's "a plan without that line skips this" clause is not surfaced in any log line.
  WHY: The report is the only observability the operator gets. Two different skip paths produce indistinguishable report
